newsitem.title: USA: U.S. Plains fed cattle market slow at $67 - trade.
newsitem.headline: U.S. Plains fed cattle market slow at $67 - trade.

text.p: U.S. Plains feedlot cattle markets Thursday were slow at $67.00 per cwt amid light inquiry, down $1.00 from the bulk of this week's activity, feedlot sources said.

About 100 head sold in the Texas Panhandle and western Oklahoma area and about 300 to 500 sold in Kansas, but not enough slaughter steers or heifers were confirmed for an adequate market test, according to USDA.
The market was starting to lean lower following steep declines this week in beef prices, the feedlot sources said.
Beef prices at midday were quoted down $0.50 to $0.97 per cwt, with 242 fabricated loads sold, according to USDA. The heavyweight choice value was down $0.97 at $108.36, down $6.58 since last Friday.
Declines were tied to increased beef supplies that offset moderate to heavy sales, market sources said.
